title: Ethics in IT
subtitle: Rapid-fire review — faster correct answers score more

questions.q: The utilitarian ethical framework judges the morality of an action primarily by which criterion?
options: Whether the action reflects the actor's virtuous character
Whether the action follows a universal moral rule
The rights the action either protects or violates
The consequences the action produces for the greatest number of people
questions.note: Utilitarianism, associated with Bentham and Mill, evaluates actions by their outcomes -- an action is ethical if it produces the greatest good for the greatest number.

questions.q: Kant's categorical imperative requires that an ethical action must be justifiable as what?
options: A universal law that all rational agents could act upon simultaneously
The action producing the least harm to the most vulnerable party
The action a reasonable person would take under identical circumstances
An action approved by the professional body governing the field
questions.note: Kant's categorical imperative states: act only according to principles you could will to be universal laws. If an action cannot be universalized without contradiction, it is unethical.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'morally wrong but legally permissible' scenario in the IT context?
options: A developer releases a patch without authorization from the security team
A sysadmin accesses a production database without a change management ticket
A company collects and sells user behavioral data that users consented to via a lengthy terms-of-service agreement
A contractor exceeds authorized access to a client's network
questions.note: Consent buried in a long ToS may be legally valid but is widely considered ethically problematic because it exploits asymmetric information. This is a classic example of the gap between legal compliance and ethical conduct.

questions.q: The ACM Code of Ethics states that computing professionals should contribute to society and human well-being. When an IT professional's employer instructs them to deploy a system that will likely harm users, the code recommends the professional should:
options: Resign immediately without raising the issue internally
Express concern through legitimate channels and, if unresolved, consider refusing or leaving
Implement the system but document personal objections in writing
Comply, because employer obligations supersede professional codes
questions.note: The ACM Code of Ethics acknowledges that professionals must sometimes refuse harmful directives. It recommends escalating concerns through legitimate channels before refusing, and ultimately choosing professional integrity over compliance.

questions.q: The principle of 'informed consent' in IT ethics requires that users:
options: Have the technical knowledge to evaluate all possible uses of their data
Be given meaningful, understandable information about data use before agreeing
Acknowledge a privacy policy has been posted on the company's website
Opt in through any mechanism the service provider chooses
questions.note: Genuine informed consent requires comprehensible disclosure of what data is collected, how it will be used, and who it will be shared with -- before the user agrees. Burying terms in dense legalese does not meet the ethical standard.

questions.q: In 2016, Volkswagen engineers programmed diesel vehicles to detect EPA emissions tests and alter engine performance to pass. From a deontological perspective, this was unethical primarily because:
options: Engineers used their professional skills to deceive regulators and the public
The environmental harm caused exceeded the financial benefit to VW shareholders
The engineers violated their employment contracts by acting outside authorized scope
The fraud was eventually detected, making it a failed consequentialist calculation
questions.note: Deontological ethics focuses on the intrinsic nature of the act, not the outcome. Deliberately programming deception violates the duty of honesty; it is wrong regardless of whether it was discovered.

questions.q: Aristotle's concept of eudaimonia, as applied to professional ethics, suggests that an IT professional's career should be oriented toward:
options: Accumulating credentials that demonstrate technical competence
Maximizing compensation and advancement opportunities
Achieving human flourishing through the exercise of practical wisdom and virtue
Fulfilling contractual obligations to clients and employers
questions.note: Eudaimonia translates roughly as flourishing or the good life. Aristotle argued it is achieved through the consistent exercise of virtue and practical wisdom (phronesis). Applied to IT, it points toward a career built on integrity, growth, and genuine service.

questions.q: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) establishes the right of patients to control their Protected Health Information (PHI). A hospital's IT team is migrating records to a cloud vendor. Which action is ethically and legally required before the migration?
options: Encrypting all data in transit using any commercially available encryption standard
Obtaining explicit consent from each patient whose records will be migrated
Executing a Business Associate Agreement with the cloud vendor that obligates HIPAA compliance
Informing the cloud vendor of the HIPAA sensitivity before contract signing
questions.note: HIPAA requires covered entities to execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with any vendor who handles PHI. Without a BAA, the hospital is legally exposed and ethically responsible for the vendor's handling of patient data.

questions.q: A company discovers it has been collecting more user location data than it disclosed in its privacy policy -- a processing error caused the over-collection for six months. The company has not yet suffered a breach. From an ethical standpoint, what should the company do?
options: Conduct an internal audit and disclose the issue to affected users and relevant regulators
Delete the excess data quietly and update the privacy policy going forward
Wait to see if regulators notice before taking action
Retain the data indefinitely because it may have research value
questions.note: Transparency is a core privacy principle. Collecting data beyond disclosed scope is a violation of user trust. Ethical practice requires disclosure to affected users and, under regulations like GDPR or CCPA, notification to regulators even when no breach has occurred.

questions.q: A social media platform's content moderation policy removes posts it deems 'misinformation' about public health topics. Critics argue this restricts free expression. Which argument best defends the platform's action?
options: Misinformation causes no harm if users are educated enough to evaluate it critically
The government has authorized platforms to regulate health misinformation
Private companies are not bound by the First Amendment and may set their own speech rules
The platform has a legal obligation to remove harmful content under Section 230
questions.note: The First Amendment restricts government censorship, not private actors. Social media platforms, as private companies, are legally permitted to set community standards and moderate content as they see fit. Whether this is ethically wise is a separate debate.

questions.q: Under US copyright law, the doctrine of 'fair use' permits copying of copyrighted material WITHOUT the owner's permission under certain conditions. Which factor is NOT one of the four official fair use factors?
options: The intent of the original author when creating the work
The purpose and character of the use (commercial vs. educational)
The amount and substantiality of the portion used
The nature of the copyrighted work
questions.note: The four statutory fair use factors under 17 U.S.C. 107 are: (1) purpose and character of use, (2) nature of the copyrighted work, (3) amount used, (4) effect on the market. The author's original intent is not among them.

questions.q: A developer uses a short snippet of open-source code licensed under the GNU GPL in a commercial product but does not release the product's source code. What ethical and legal issue does this create?
options: The developer has violated the GPL's copyleft requirement, which mandates that derivative works be released under the same license
The developer has committed plagiarism by not crediting the original author
Using any GPL code in a commercial product is always prohibited
The developer owes licensing fees to the Free Software Foundation
questions.note: The GPL is a copyleft license: it requires that any derivative work incorporating GPL code must also be released under the GPL. Distributing a proprietary product containing GPL code without source disclosure is a license violation and an ethical breach of the open-source community's trust.

questions.q: A company collects extensive behavioral data on users and sells detailed profiles to advertisers without clearly disclosing this in its privacy policy. Which ethical principle is most directly violated?
options: The principle of data minimization
The principle of transparency and notice
The principle of purpose limitation
The principle of data accuracy
questions.note: Transparency and notice require that organizations clearly disclose what data they collect and how it will be used. Selling behavioral profiles without clear disclosure violates the user's right to know and make an informed choice, which is the foundational privacy harm in this scenario.

questions.q: A government agency proposes building a national facial recognition database to identify individuals in public spaces in real time. Which concern is MOST central to the ethical debate about this proposal?
options: The potential for the database to be breached by foreign adversaries
The chilling effect on freedom of assembly, expression, and movement created by mass surveillance
The technical accuracy rate of current facial recognition systems
The cost of deploying and maintaining the infrastructure at national scale
questions.note: While accuracy, cost, and security are real concerns, the core ethical issue is the impact on civil liberties. When citizens know they are being identified and tracked in public, they may self-censor and avoid lawful activities -- a chilling effect that undermines the freedoms a democratic society is meant to protect.

questions.q: A QA engineer discovers a known defect in a medical device's firmware that could cause incorrect dosage calculations in rare conditions. The release date is one week away and fixing the bug would delay it by three months. The project manager pressures the team to ship. The engineer should:
options: Disclose the defect to the FDA before the release date without informing management
Escalate the concern formally in writing and refuse to certify the release until the safety-critical defect is resolved
Document the defect and ship on schedule, noting the risk in the post-release backlog
Calculate the statistical probability of the defect occurring and defer only if the probability exceeds 1%
questions.note: Safety-critical software defects that can harm users cannot be resolved by probability calculations or release pressure. The engineer has a professional and ethical obligation to formally escalate the concern. In regulated industries, shipping with a known safety defect may also be illegal.

questions.q: A team is building a predictive hiring algorithm to screen resumes. Internal testing shows it performs with 85% accuracy overall but rejects candidates from historically underrepresented groups at twice the rate of other groups. The ethically correct response is:
options: Halt deployment, audit the training data for bias, and redesign the model before use in consequential decisions
Deploy the system because an 85% accuracy rate exceeds the human recruiter benchmark
Deploy with a human override option for any candidate who requests a manual review
Disclose the disparity rate in the product's technical documentation and proceed
questions.note: Disparate impact -- where a neutral-seeming system produces unequal outcomes for protected groups -- is a recognized form of discrimination. An 85% accuracy rate that achieves that score partly by systematically disadvantaging a group is not ethically acceptable. The training data and model must be audited.

questions.q: The digital divide refers to which social concern?
options: The growing complexity of systems that makes them inaccessible to non-expert users
The difference in software quality between open-source and proprietary systems
The gap in security posture between large enterprises and small businesses
Unequal access to technology, internet connectivity, and digital literacy across socioeconomic and geographic groups
questions.note: The digital divide describes the unequal distribution of access to information technology, including hardware, broadband internet, and the skills to use them effectively. It amplifies existing social and economic inequalities when essential services and opportunities move online.

questions.q: A developer is asked to build a feature that allows an app to access the user's location continuously in the background, even when the app is not in use. The business justification is advertising personalization. The most ethical design approach is:
options: Refuse to build it, as the data collection purpose does not justify the privacy intrusion
Implement it only if the app's privacy policy is updated before the next release cycle
Implement it with the ability for users to opt out in settings, buried two levels deep in the menu
Implement the feature as requested because location data is a legitimate business asset
questions.note: Continuous background location tracking for advertising is a disproportionate privacy intrusion relative to the purpose. The principle of data minimization holds that only data necessary for a stated, legitimate purpose should be collected. Advertising personalization does not meet that bar for continuous background location access.

questions.q: When a software company issues a silent update that changes product functionality users relied upon -- without any notification -- this primarily violates which principle?
options: The principle of data integrity, because the update may alter stored user data
The principle of least privilege, because the update may expand the application's system access
The principle of informed consent and transparency, because users were not notified of changes affecting their use
The principle of availability, because the update may introduce downtime
questions.note: Silent changes to product behavior undermine user trust and informed consent. Users who adopt a product based on its capabilities have a reasonable expectation that significant changes will be communicated. The ethical obligation to be transparent applies to product changes as well as data practices.

questions.q: The concept of 'technoethics' as described by the Reynolds textbook argues that:
options: Only licensed engineers should be permitted to make ethical judgments about technology systems
Technology is inherently neutral and ethical concerns belong to the humans who deploy it, not the technology itself
The pace of technological change makes traditional ethical frameworks obsolete
Ethics must be embedded into the design, development, and governance of technology systems from the outset
questions.note: Technoethics holds that technology is not neutral -- design decisions encode values, and those values have consequences. Ethical reasoning must be integrated throughout the lifecycle of technology development, not applied retroactively after harm occurs.
